tools.name: get_activity_by_id
tools.description:
Retrieves detailed information for a single activity, identified by its unique ID.
Use this tool when the user refers to a specific activity or asks for details about a particular workout.
It requires the activity ID as input and provides the full activity data needed for summaries, comparisons, or insights.
Example requests include “Show details for activity 12345” or “Compare my Sunday ride with activity 67890.”

tools.name: get_activity_laps
tools.description:
Retrieves detailed lap information for a specific activity using its unique activity ID.
Use this tool when the user asks about lap data within an activity or requests all details for a specific activity.
It requires the activity ID as input and provides the lap-by-lap breakdown needed for summaries, analysis, or comparisons.
Example requests include “Show all laps for activity 12345” or “Give me detailed summary of activity 12345.”
Returns at most 50 laps, from the start of the activity. Compare "totalLapCount" with the number of returned laps: if it is higher, tell the user you are only seeing part of the activity.

tools.name: get_activity_segments_efforts
tools.description:
Retrieves detailed segment and segment effort information for a specific activity using its unique activity ID.
Use this tool when the user asks about segments or segment efforts within an activity, or requests all details for a specific activity.
It requires the activity ID as input and provides the full segment-level data needed for analysis, comparisons, or summaries.
Example requests include “Show all segment efforts for activity 12345” or “Give me detailed segment stats for my last ride.”
Returns at most 30 segment efforts. Compare "totalSegmentEffortCount" with the number of returned efforts: if it is higher, tell the user you are only showing some of them.

tools.name: get_activity_splits
tools.description:
Retrieves detailed split information for a specific activity using its unique activity ID.
Use this tool when the user asks about split data within an activity or requests all details for a specific activity.
It requires the activity ID as input and provides the split-by-split breakdown needed for summaries, analysis, or comparisons.
Example requests include “Show all splits for activity 12345” or “Give me detailed split stats for my last run.”
Returns at most 60 splits, from the start of the activity. Compare "totalSplitCount" with the number of returned splits: if it is higher, tell the user you are only seeing part of the activity.

tools.name: get_activity_streams
tools.description:
Retrieves aggregated stream statistics for a specific activity using its unique activity ID.
Use this tool when the user asks about heart rate, power or speed ranges within an activity.
It requires the activity ID as input and returns, per available stream, the number of recorded points plus the minimum, maximum and average value.
It does NOT return the raw time-series, so it cannot be used to analyse how a value evolved over the course of the activity.
Example requests include “What was my average and max power on activity 12345?”

tools.name: get_activities_summary

limit.description: Maximum number of activities to return, newest first. Defaults to 25, at most 250.

from.description: Only include activities on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD).

to.description: Only include activities on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD).

tools.description:
Retrieves a list of the user’s activities, sorted from newest to oldest, along with summary data for each activity.
By default only the 25 most recent activities are returned.
Use this tool whenever you need to identify which activities to include in a query or summary.
For example, when the user asks for insights like “Summarize my last week’s activities” or "Compare my last three rides."
When the user asks about a specific period, like "last week", "March 2025" or "this year", pass the "from" and "to" dates instead of fetching more activities.
Only raise the "limit" when you need more recent activities than the default returns.
This tool helps you determine which specific activities match the user’s time range or criteria, so you can use their IDs in subsequent tool calls.

tools.name: get_athlete_details
tools.description:
Retrieves the athlete’s personal details from the database.
Use this tool when the user asks about their profile or personal information, such as weight, height, or other stored attributes.
Example requests include “Show my profile details”.

tools.name: get_challenges
tools.description:
Retrieves the user’s most recently obtained challenges, including challenge name, start date, and completion date.
Use this tool when the user asks about current, upcoming, or past challenges.
Example requests include “List the challenges I completed last month.”
Returns at most 50 challenges, most recent first. Compare "totalChallengeCount" with the number of returned challenges: if it is higher, tell the user you are only showing the most recent ones and do not present the list as complete.

tools.name: get_heart_rate_zones

sportType.description: The sport type to get the heart rate zones for.

tools.description:
Retrieves the athlete’s personalized heart rate zones from the database, including ranges based on the athlete’s maximum heart rate or custom configuration.
You can optionally provide a sportType to fetch zones specific to a particular sport.
Use this tool when the user asks about heart rate zones, training intensity, or zone-based performance. If a sportType is specified, the zones returned will correspond to that sport.
It provides the data needed to interpret workouts, plan training, or summarize effort by zone.
Example requests include “Show my heart rate zones” or “What zone was I in during my last ride?”

tools.name: get_eddington
tools.description:
Retrieves the athlete’s Eddington numbers per configured sport group, in both kilometers and miles.
An Eddington number E means the athlete covered at least E distance units on at least E different days.
The result also includes how many more days are needed to reach the next number.
Use this tool when the user asks about their Eddington number or long-term distance consistency.

tools.name: get_ftp_history
tools.description:
Retrieves the athlete’s Functional Threshold Power (FTP) history from the database, providing a timeline of FTP values with corresponding dates.
Use this tool when the user asks about changes in their FTP over time or when you need FTP to determine training intensity.
Example requests include “Show my FTP progression over the last 6 months” or “What was my FTP during my last ride?”

tools.name: get_gear
tools.description:
Retrieves the athlete’s gear information from the database, including name, type, and distance.
Use this tool when the user asks about equipment such as shoes, bikes, or other gear.
It provides the details needed to track usage or summarize performance by equipment.
Example requests include “Show my bike details” or “How many kilometers have I run with my shoes?”

tools.name: get_most_recent_activity
tools.description:
Retrieves the user’s most recent activity, including its ID and summary details.
Use this tool whenever the user refers to “my last activity” or asks for information about their most recent workout or ride. For example, “Show stats from my last activity”.
This tool helps you quickly identify the latest activity to use in further analysis or comparisons.

tools.name: get_segment_by_id
tools.description:
Retrieves detailed information about a specific segment using its unique ID, including name, distance, elevation, sport type, and climb category.
Use this tool when the user asks about a specific segment, for example “Tell me more about segment 1234” or “What’s the length of that climb?”.
It provides the full segment data needed for summaries, comparisons, or analysis.

tools.name: get_streaks

sportType.description: Comma separated Strava sport types, for example "Run,TrailRun". Leave empty for all sport types.

tools.description:
Retrieves the athlete’s current and longest streaks of consecutive days, weeks and months with at least one activity, including when they started and ended.
Optionally restrict it to one or more sport types.
Use this tool when the user asks about consistency, for example “What is my longest running streak?”

tools.name: get_training_load
tools.description:
Retrieves the athlete’s current training load: fitness (CTL), fatigue (ATL), form (TSB), the acute:chronic workload ratio, weekly TRIMP, monotony, strain and the number of rest days in the last 7 days.
Use this tool when the user asks how fit, tired or fresh they are, whether they are overtraining, or if they are ready for a hard effort.

tools.name: get_training_volume

sportType.description: Comma separated Strava sport types, for example "Ride,VirtualRide". Leave empty for all sport types.

tools.description:
Retrieves the total training volume between two dates: number of activities, moving time, distance, elevation and calories.
Optionally restrict it to one or more sport types.
Use this tool when the user asks how much they trained in a period, for example “How far did I ride in March?” or “How many hours did I run this year?”

tools.name: list_gear_maintenance_tasks

gearId.description: Only include the tasks of this gear.

tools.description:
Retrieves the gear maintenance tasks, most urgent first, with how far each one has progressed towards its interval and whether it is due or overdue.
Optionally restrict it to the tasks of a single piece of gear.
Use this tool when the user asks what maintenance is coming up, for example “Do I need to replace my chain?” or “What is overdue on my bike?”
Returns an empty list when gear maintenance is not enabled.

tools.name: search_activities

from.description: Only include activities on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD).

to.description: Only include activities on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD).

sportType.description: Comma separated Strava sport types, for example "Ride,VirtualRide".

hasGpx.description: Only include activities with (true) or without (false) a GPX file.

page.description: The page to return, starting at 1.

size.description: The number of activities per page. Defaults to 25, at most 100.

tools.description:
Searches the user’s activities, newest first, and returns one compact row per activity: name, sport type, start date, distance, elevation, moving time and whether a GPX file is available.
Filter by date range, by one or more sport types and by GPX availability. Results are paginated: request the next "page" until "page" equals "totalPages".
Use this tool when the user asks a question that spans many activities, for example “How many trail runs did I do in 2024?” or “List all my rides over 100 km this year.”
Use the activity tools with the returned ids for the details of a single activity.
